newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds recover, seen narrowly rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds recover, seen narrowly rangebound.

text.p: Danish bond prices continued to recover on Friday, with the 10-year Danish-German yield gap shrinking due to foreign investor interest in mortgage credit paper and better than expected local CPI data with dealers seeing narrowly rangebound prices.
Denmark's February year-on-year CPI was 2.2 percent up using the domestic method of calculation, better than analysts' 2.4 percent expectations and January's 2.7 percent.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.15 point from the opening at 108.71, yielding 6.67 percent in turnover of four billion crowns.
The 2006 benchmark's March future was untraded at 110.65. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.52 point to 87.95.
The crown traded at 3.8130 per mark at 1230 gmt, down a tad from around 3.8125 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed two basis points to 78.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of some 500 million crowns worth of medium-term state bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
